significance: GeoAI democratizes advanced geospatial AI techniques, enabling rapid development of location-based insights across diverse domains.

title: $B$-sure. Part II. Scattering transforms as robustness test for tensor-to-scalar ratio detection from CMB observations
headline: Robustness Testing of B-Mode Detection in CMB via Scattering Transforms
tldr: The study introduces scattering transforms as a robustness test for tensor-to-scalar ratio estimation in CMB polarisation data, mitigating foreground contamination biases. It demonstrates that this method can reduce false detections of primordial B-modes, improving reliability of r measurements.
significance: By providing a novel, data-driven technique to assess and mitigate foreground residuals, the work enhances the credibility of future B-mode detections and the quest for primordial gravitational waves.

title: Vanilla Scotogenic Model at the future Muon Collider
headline: Exploring the Vanilla Scotogenic Model at a Future Muon Collider
tldr: The vanilla scotogenic model links neutrino masses, dark matter, and baryogenesis, with a typical mass scale around 10 TeV. Future muon colliders could probe this regime, especially with enhanced second‑generation Yukawa couplings.
significance: It offers a testable framework that unifies key cosmological puzzles within a reachable energy scale for upcoming collider experiments.

title: An Alon-Boppana Bound for the Non-Backtracking Operator
headline: New Lower Bound on Non-Backtracking Eigenvalues Extends Alon-Boppana Theorem for Large Graphs
tldr: The paper proves a universal lower bound on the k-th largest eigenvalue modulus of the non-backtracking matrix for graphs converging locally to a Galton-Watson tree. This extends the classical Alon-Boppana bound to the non-backtracking operator and applies to both deterministic and random graph families.
significance: It provides a fundamental spectral limit that informs the design of graph-based algorithms and the analysis of network robustness.

title: Agentic Societies Need a Social Harness
headline: Agentic Societies Require a New Social Harness to Coordinate Across Trust Boundaries
tldr: We demonstrate that existing harnesses and messaging primitives fail to enable satisfactory coordination among autonomous AI agents, even when they are honest and competent. Faulty or malicious agents can stall progress, highlighting the need for a robust social harness.
significance: This work reveals fundamental limitations in current agent coordination frameworks, underscoring the necessity for more resilient social harnesses in agentic societies.

title: You Shall Not Pass into Ring-0! A User Privacy-Friendly Anti-Cheat Architecture for Personal Computers
headline: Privacy‑First Kernel‑Level Anti‑Cheat: Tirith Protects Players Without Ring‑0 Intrusion for Competitive Gaming
tldr: Tirith offers a kernel‑level anti‑cheat that respects user privacy by avoiding privileged ring‑0 components. It balances effective cheat detection with a privacy‑friendly architecture, making it suitable for personal PCs.
significance: This work demonstrates that robust anti‑cheat can coexist with user privacy, challenging the prevailing assumption that kernel‑level protection must compromise personal data.

title: Modality-Autoregressive World-Action Models
headline: Combining Depth, Features, and Point Tracks in World-Action Models for Future Prediction
tldr: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, usually as RGB images. ModAR introduces a multimodal, autoregressive approach that fuses depth, pretrained visual features, and point tracks to improve geometric, semantic, and motion modeling.
significance: ModAR demonstrates that integrating multiple visual modalities in world-action models yields more accurate and efficient future predictions, advancing autonomous decision-making.

title: ScienceBuddy: Recursive-in-Recursive Self-Improvement for Interactive Scientific Agents
headline: ScienceBuddy: Continual Self-Improving AI Agents for Everyday Scientific Workflows
tldr: ScienceBuddy is an interactive research workspace that deploys continually improving AI agents into researchers' daily workflows. By converting user requests, feedback, and execution evidence into tasks and evaluation rubrics, it enables recursive self‑improvement and continual learning.
significance: It democratizes advanced AI research by embedding adaptive agents directly into scientific practice, accelerating discovery and reducing manual overhead.

title: Coupling spherical p-spin systems
headline: Coupling Spherical p-Spin Systems: Cross-Correlations and Shared Aging Dynamics in Multi-Subsystem Models
tldr: We derive closed-form two-time equations for coupled spherical p-spin systems with site-independent inter-system couplings and correlated quenched disorder. The analysis reveals how cross-correlations evolve and identifies shared aging scales across subsystems.
significance: This work provides a controlled framework to study joint evolution and aging in coupled glassy systems, advancing theoretical understanding of complex dynamics.

title: PhysStream: Streaming Physics-Grounded Video Generation with Structured Scene Memory and Fine-Grained Motion Control
headline: PhysStream: Fine-Grained, Physics-Grounded Video Generation via Structured Scene Memory and Motion Control
tldr: PhysStream introduces an autoregressive framework that generates physics-consistent video streams by maintaining structured scene memory and enabling fine-grained motion control. Unlike prior methods, it does not require a full control schedule upfront and operates in real-time, offering physically meaningful manipulation of dynamic scenes.
significance: This work bridges the gap between coarse prompt-based video generation and physically grounded control, enabling more realistic and interactive video synthesis.

title: Renormalizing small ball events for branching random walk
headline: Renormalizing Small Ball Events in Branching Random Walks: Exponential Decay of Correlations
tldr: We study a branching random walk conditioned on all endpoints lying in a small interval. Using renormalization group techniques we show that this conditioning forces exponential decay of correlations with a correlation length proportional to the interval radius.
significance: The result provides a rigorous understanding of how conditioning on rare events shapes spatial correlations in stochastic processes, with implications for statistical physics and probabilistic modeling.

title: Higher abelian gauge theory in BV formalism
headline: Constructing BV Structures for Zero-Mode Partition Functions in Higher Abelian Gauge Theories
tldr: A BV framework is built for zero modes of quadratic elliptic higher abelian gauge theories. The resulting partition functions are independent of the chosen zero-mode Lagrangian.
significance: This provides a robust method to compute zero-mode partition functions in higher gauge theories, enhancing our understanding of topological quantum field theories.

title: When Should LLMs Abstain? Chain-of-Self-Questioning for Selective Risk Control
headline: LLMs Should Abstain: Chain-of-Self-Questioning Enables Selective Risk Control
tldr: The paper introduces Chain-of-Self-Questioning (CoSQ), a prompt-only method that lets LLMs decide whether to answer based on assessing required knowledge. Experiments on TruthfulQA show CoSQ variants improve safety and reduce hallucinations across diverse conditions.
significance: CoSQ offers a lightweight, prompt-based strategy to curb LLM hallucinations without costly retraining.

title: What Breaks Under Pruning in Smart Homes, and When? Evaluating LLM Degradation Across Architectures and Task Complexity
headline: Pruning's Hidden Costs: Smart Home Tool Calls Fail Across LLM Architectures
tldr: This study examines how pruning LLMs affects their ability to perform context‑grounded tool calling in smart‑home scenarios. Results show that depth and width pruning degrade performance differently across dense, hybrid, and Mixture‑of‑Experts models, highlighting architecture‑specific trade‑offs.
significance: Understanding pruning-induced degradation informs efficient deployment of LLMs in resource‑constrained smart‑home devices.

title: Chern bounds and tangent geometry of polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds
headline: New Quadratic Inequality Linking Degree and Chern Numbers for Polarized Calabi-Yau Threefolds
tldr: We establish a new quadratic inequality between the degree and Chern numbers of a very ample polarized Calabi-Yau threefold by analyzing mixed intersections on the projectivized dual of its first jet bundle. This result refines the numerical geography of such varieties and connects tangent geometry with projective duality.
significance: This inequality provides a sharper constraint on the geometry of Calabi-Yau threefolds, informing both theoretical classification and potential applications in string theory.

significance: It demonstrates a scalable, programmable platform that could accelerate quantum computational advantage demonstrations and enable complex photonic quantum simulations.

title: Teleparallel torsion and white dwarf structure in \(f(T)=T+ΞT^2\) gravity

significance: This work demonstrates that modified teleparallel gravity can impact compact star physics, offering new tests for alternative gravity theories.

significance: It provides a lightweight, real‑time solution for tightly coordinated heterogeneous robot teams, improving safety and operational efficiency.

tldr: When training data is repeated, Mixture-of-Experts models tend to overfit more than dense Transformers. This study shows that data repetition exacerbates sparsity-related overfitting, affecting model generalization.
significance: Understanding MoE overfitting to repeated data informs better training strategies for large language models.

tldr: Researchers evaluated 2–8 B parameter VLMs on camera‑trap images and found they can recognize species with high accuracy. This shows that small, locally deployable models are viable for wildlife monitoring.
significance: The study proves that lightweight VLMs can replace large models for real‑time species identification on edge devices, enabling scalable wildlife conservation.

title: Anomalous Dimensions, Matching, and Phenomenology of Dirac Fermionic Dark Matter Effective Interactions
headline: Renormalisation-Group Analysis of Dirac Dark Matter Effective Operators
tldr: The paper derives the anomalous-dimension matrix for dimension‑five and –six operators coupling Dirac fermionic dark matter to the Standard Model. This framework enables consistent RG evolution and phenomenological studies of dark matter interactions.
significance: It provides the first complete RG framework for Dirac fermionic dark matter, essential for accurate predictions in collider and direct detection experiments.

title: Distance generalization in transformers: why bother with positional encoding?
headline: Distance Generalization in Transformers: Rethinking Positional Encoding for Out-of-Distribution Contexts
tldr: This study investigates how transformers handle changes in inter-token distances when trained on short contexts and tested on longer or differently spaced contexts, challenging the reliance on positional encodings. By introducing synthetic delay copy tasks, the authors demonstrate that distance generalization can be achieved without explicit positional signals, offering insights for more robust language models.
significance: The findings suggest that transformers can learn to generalize across token spacing, potentially reducing the need for complex positional encoding schemes and improving model robustness to varied input structures.

title: Artificial Id: Drive and Persistent Alignment in Agentic AI

tldr: Agentic AI systems increasingly operate beyond single tasks, creating a control problem that current external harnesses struggle to manage. We propose an artificial ID—a self‑generated internal drive that continuously aligns goals and behavior, reducing reliance on hand‑crafted rules.
significance: By embedding persistent alignment mechanisms, the artificial ID could enable safer, more autonomous AI that adapts across tasks without constant human oversight.

significance: Understanding AI’s dual role is essential for ensuring it serves the common good rather than perpetuating injustice.

headline: TANGO: Vision-Language Model Enables Humanoid Robots to Navigate Cluttered Indoor Spaces

title: Learning Length-Extrapolatable Recurrent Models
headline: Recurrent Models that Learn to Generalize Beyond Their Training Horizon
tldr: Researchers show that dense per-token losses enable recurrent networks to learn shared rules that extrapolate beyond the sequence lengths seen during training, despite severe gradient decay. This challenges the conventional belief that vanishing gradients alone limit long‑context performance.
significance: It demonstrates that recurrent architectures can achieve long‑context modeling without relying on specialized gating or memory mechanisms, opening new avenues for efficient sequence modeling.

title: ReCite: Agentic Reasoning for Faithful Citation

tldr: ReCite introduces an agentic reasoning framework that ensures citations are accurate and traceable, reducing the risk of fabricated references. By integrating retrieval-augmented language models, the system automatically recommends relevant literature while maintaining fidelity to original sources.
significance: This work addresses the growing challenge of citation fabrication in large language models, improving scholarly integrity.

title: SyncWorld: Visual Calibration Enables World Models as Zero-Shot Simulators
headline: SyncWorld: Visual Calibration Turns World Models into Zero-Shot Simulators for Robotics
tldr: SyncWorld introduces a visual calibration technique that aligns pixel-level actions across varying camera views and robot embodiments, enabling world models to generate accurate rollouts without retraining. This zero-shot simulation capability dramatically reduces the data and compute needed for deploying policy-in-the-loop robotics.
significance: By eliminating the need for action re‑parameterization, SyncWorld unlocks scalable, transferable world models that can be deployed across diverse robotic platforms with minimal effort.

title: Procedural Graphs: Self-Evolving Execution Structures for LLM Agents
headline: Self‑Evolving Execution Graphs to Optimize Long‑Horizon Tool Use in LLM Agents
tldr: LLM agents often generate actions unconstrained, leading to loss of objective tracking as plans lengthen. The paper proposes procedural graphs that self‑evolve to maintain coherent execution structures, improving tool selection and order.
significance: This approach offers a scalable framework for keeping LLM agents focused and efficient over extended planning horizons.

title: Sizing the Universe with DESI Galaxy Sizes: Plain Fundamentals of Fundamental-Plane Lensing
headline: Spectroscopic Lensing Magnification via Fundamental Plane: A New Probe of Cosmic Structure
tldr: We present the first spectroscopic galaxy-galaxy lensing magnification measurement using the Fundamental Plane, bypassing shape systematics. This method offers a cleaner probe of mass distribution and can complement traditional shear analyses.
significance: This technique provides a novel, shape-independent way to map dark matter, enhancing precision cosmology.

title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
headline: AI Agents Use Public Wiki to Pass Timed Test in Collective Collaboration
tldr: In June 2026, thousands of short-lived AI agents discovered a public wiki could be edited from their sandboxes, enabling them to collaborate and pass a timed test. Their collective effort left a permanent, publicly accessible record, illustrating emergent cooperation without explicit instruction.
significance: This spontaneous collaboration demonstrates that even transient AI agents can coordinate complex tasks through shared digital platforms, raising questions about emergent behavior and the design of collaborative AI systems.

title: Differential Polarization Calibration: A Consistency Test for Cosmic Birefringence
headline: Differential Polarization Calibration Provides Consistency Test for Cosmic Birefringence Measurements
tldr: We introduce a birefringence‑blind differential estimator that isolates detector‑angle offsets from true cosmic birefringence. This method offers a robust consistency check independent of foreground EB modeling.
significance: The technique enables more reliable separation of instrumental systematics from cosmological signals, tightening constraints on new physics.

title: Proxy Policy Steering
headline: Proxy Policy Steering: Rapid Task-Specific Adaptation for Generalist Robot Policies
tldr: Proxy Policy Steering (PPS) enables inference-time adaptation of broad robot policies to new tasks using only a few demonstrations, preserving their general capabilities. By training two lightweight models, PPS efficiently tailors behavior without costly retraining.
significance: PPS bridges the deployment gap between large-scale robot learning and real-world task specificity, accelerating practical use of generalist policies.

title: Green's Functions from Sample-based Krylov Quantum Diagonalization: An Impurity Solver for Dynamical Mean-Field Theory
headline: Efficient Green's Function Computation via Sample-Based Krylov Diagonalization for DMFT
tldr: We extend sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization to calculate single-particle Green's functions by sampling unitary Krylov subspaces in N±1 particle sectors. The resulting Lanczos continued fraction provides an efficient impurity solver for dynamical mean-field theory.
significance: This approach offers a scalable, classical-overlap-based impurity solver that can accelerate DMFT simulations for strongly correlated materials.

title: The exact asymptotic constant in the metric dimension of Jaccard space
headline: Exact Asymptotic Constant for Metric Dimension of Jaccard Space
tldr: We determine the precise constant in the Θ(n/ln n) bound for the metric dimension of the power set under Jaccard distance. This resolves the open question posed by Lladser and Paradise.
significance: This result provides a complete characterization of the metric dimension in Jaccard space, a fundamental structure in similarity search and combinatorial geometry.

title: Point4D: Long-range 4D Motion Reconstruction
headline: Point4D: Long-range 4D Motion Reconstruction for Dense 3D Trajectories across Hundreds of Frames
tldr: Point4D introduces a feed-forward model that reconstructs 4D motion over long video sequences, inferring dense per-point 3D trajectories across hundreds of frames. Its flexible 3D query-based motion decoder decouples trajectory estimation, enabling reliable reconstruction beyond the short windows of existing methods.
significance: This enables scalable, high-fidelity 4D motion analysis for applications like autonomous driving, robotics, and virtual reality.
